title: Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act
official_title: To establish fraud prevention and program integrity functions and data sharing authorities within the Department of Treasury and a permanent governmentwide Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Sessions (R-TX) with 1 cosponsor; passed the House. Anti-fraud oversight tends to attract bipartisan interest, but creating a new Senate-confirmed Inspector General and Treasury data role is a larger lift, and the bill needs 60 votes in the Senate with key provisions delayed to 2028.
summary: Stands up a new permanent, Senate-confirmed Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery inside the Treasury, gives the Treasury's Fiscal Service a governmentwide fraud-data analysis role, and folds in the pandemic-era oversight committee's assets.
brief: Creates a permanent governmentwide fraud Inspector General and fraud-data functions inside the Treasury.

top_lines.headline: New Governmentwide Fraud Inspector General
subs: Creates a permanent IG for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery in the Treasury
Presidential appointment with Senate confirmation; oversight of "covered funds"
$10M authorized annually beginning in fiscal year 2035

top_lines.headline: Treasury Fiscal Service Fraud Role
subs: Bureau of the Fiscal Service runs the Do Not Pay system and a governmentwide data-analysis program
Makes the DATA Act analysis center mandatory ('may' becomes 'shall')
Functions explicitly exclude any investigative or law-enforcement role

top_lines.headline: Pandemic Oversight Wound Down Into the New Office
subs: Ends the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee on December 31, 2028 (moved up from 2034)
Transfers PRAC's assets, data, and staff to the new office
Treasury must flag fraud risks in any relief bill over $100B or new program over $100M

items.main: Names the Act the “Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Fraud Prevention and Financial Integrity Functions in Treasury

items.main: Rewrites the Fiscal Service's statutory functions around fraud prevention, data analysis, and improper-payment prevention.
items.detail: Rewrites section 306 of title 31, U.S. Code. The Bureau of the Fiscal Service maintains financial-integrity, spending-transparency, and improper-payment-prevention functions — explicitly excluding any investigative or law-enforcement function. It administers the Do Not Pay system and establishes a governmentwide data-analysis program (using the DATA Act's authority) that shares data and analysis with federal agencies, states, and nongovernmental entities, requires agencies to share known or suspected fraud data and to screen awardees and payees against a centralized fraud database, and provides the new Inspector General access to data. The Treasury must report to Congress within 2 years and annually thereafter, and the bill makes the DATA Act data-analysis center mandatory by changing 'may' to 'shall.'

sections.label: Section 3 — Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery

items.main: Establishes a permanent, Senate-confirmed Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery within the Treasury.
items.detail: Adds section 317 to title 31. The Inspector General is appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate, without regard to political affiliation, and oversees 'covered funds' through audits and investigations, support to agency Inspectors General, an independent data-analytics platform (incorporating the platform built by the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee), coordination with the Department of Justice, an advisory committee of Inspectors General, and reporting suspected criminal violations to the Attorney General. The office may hire staff, employ annuitants, and enter contracts. The bill authorizes $10M annually beginning in fiscal year 2035, transfers the PRAC's assets and obligations to the office, and takes effect on December 31, 2028.

sections.label: Section 4 — Data Sharing for Fraud Prevention

items.main: Gives the Treasury authority to negotiate data-sharing agreements and to flag fraud risks in large spending measures.
items.detail: Amends section 321(a) of title 31 to let the Treasury enter memoranda of understanding with federal agencies, Inspectors General, law enforcement, and private entities to secure data access for fraud and improper-payment prevention. For any supplemental or emergency relief measure totaling more than $100B, or any new program with more than $100M in anticipated additional annual spending, the Treasury must give Congress's leadership and the relevant committees legislative recommendations so that existing fraud-prevention functions are used or expanded rather than duplicated and adequate resources are provided. OMB must issue implementing guidance within 270 days.

sections.label: Section 5 — Termination and Transfer of PRAC Assets

items.main: Winds the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee down into the new office.
items.detail: Amends the CARES Act to move the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee's termination date up from September 30, 2034 to December 31, 2028. On that date, the committee's assets and obligations — including contracts, data, records, unobligated balances, and identified personnel — transfer to the new Office of the Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery, and CARES Act section 15010 is repealed.

underreported: The new office would inherit the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee's data-analytics platform, assets, and personnel rather than starting from scratch.

criticisms.why: you will not hear anything more rich in this body today than listening to a Democrat who did absolutely nothing about fraud for the last 4 years talk about why we should oppose a very good measure to prevent and oppose fraud. Madam Speaker, I yield 7 minutes to the gentleman from Texas (Mr. Sessions), the sponsor of this good legislation.

Mr. Comer has begun telling the story about H.R. 8312, Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act, which we today will discuss, but I think it is important that we probably tell a story because this has two tales, but one truth to it. The bottom line is that our friends, if they oppose this today, it is because they are embarrassed.

gaps: The new Inspector General’s funding is not authorized until fiscal year 2035, though the office and its duties take effect December 31, 2028.
'Covered funds' is defined by a fixed list of pandemic-era and other laws plus federal awards of $50,000 or more, with expansion left to future legislation.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Boebert
featured_quotes.text: The American people expect their government to be a responsible steward of taxpayer dollars, yet every year, the Federal Government loses hundreds of billions of dollars to fraud, waste, and abuse of our hard-earned money. While the Federal Government provides families, workers, and businesses with the support they need, several COVID-era spending programs exposed serious weaknesses in our ability to prevent fraud. Once those dollars were lost, it has proven to be nearly impossible to recover them.

added: A permanent, Senate-confirmed Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery within the Treasury ($10M authorized annually from fiscal year 2035); a governmentwide fraud-data analysis program in the Fiscal Service; a Treasury duty to recommend fraud safeguards for relief bills over $100B or new programs over $100M
modified: Rewrites the Fiscal Service's statutory functions (31 U.S.C. 306) around fraud prevention and data analysis; makes the DATA Act data-analysis center mandatory; moves the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee's sunset up to December 31, 2028
removed: The Pandemic Response Accountability Committee (repealed December 31, 2028, with its assets transferred to the new office)

added: State definition for the data program expanded inline to include the District of Columbia, territories/possessions, and federally recognized Indian Tribes
modified: Treasury Fiscal Service governmentwide data analysis program changed from mandatory to a 'voluntary' program, facilitating services 'upon request and on a voluntary basis in accordance with all applicable privacy and security laws'

Agency data-sharing reframed from mandatory commands ('requiring each agency to share/screen') to voluntary services agencies may request — and added 'but for no other purpose including any policy analysis and enforcement action purpose'

Fraud-data sharing narrowed to entities 'resulting from final adverse action determinations, payment denials, referrals for criminal investigation, or equivalent findings' rather than from any internal agency investigation
Inspector General access to Treasury IT/data (sec. 306(c)(3)) now simply 'in accordance with applicable law' instead of subject to a Secretary discretion-to-deny carve-out with congressional notice
Sec. 4(a)(10) data-access authority reworded to 'agreements with private entities' (was 'and private entities') as may be appropriate
